Adversarially verify this code-review finding from the M12 diff. Read the actual code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default to isReal=false if it's a false positive, pre-existing, out of scope, or already handled.

Lens: a11y
Severity: medium
File: app/(customer)/account/page.tsx (Receipts StatusBadge, lines 174-178: <StatusBadge>{p.status}</StatusBadge>)
Title: Payment status rendered as raw machine enum, unlocalized and read verbatim
Detail: The badge prints p.status directly, so the payment_status enum values "authorized" / "captured" / "refunded" / "failed" (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:634) are shown as-is and spoken verbatim by a screen reader. This is a raw token rather than human-readable copy and violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing strings via messages/en.json) — every other status in the diff (bookings, availability) goes through a localized label map. Additionally a "failed" payment renders with tone="neutral" (grey), so a failure is not visually distinguished from a normal non-captured state; meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.
Suggestion: Add a status->message map (e.g. account.payStatusCaptured / Authorized / Refunded / Failed) and render the localized label. Map "failed" to tone="alert" so the visual treatment matches the meaning and isn't carried by text alone.

All claims are verified. Let me consolidate my findings.

**Verification results:**

1. **Raw enum rendered verbatim** — CONFIRMED. Line 177 `{p.status}` renders the `payment_status` enum (`"authorized" | "captured" | "refunded" | "failed"`, confirmed at database.types.ts:633) directly. No localization, no label map. A screen reader will read "captured", "authorized", "refunded", or "failed" verbatim as lowercase machine tokens.

2. **Violates CLAUDE.md rule 7** — CONFIRMED. Every other user-facing string on the page goes through `t(...)` / `messages/en.json`. There are NO payment-status keys in en.json (grep returned none). This is a genuine raw-string-in-component violation, newly introduced in M12 (the `+` lines in the diff confirm this is new code).

3. **"failed" renders grey (tone="neutral")** — CONFIRMED. Line 175: `tone={p.status === "captured" ? "success" : "neutral"}`. Only "captured" gets a distinct (success/green) tone; "authorized", "refunded", AND "failed" all collapse to neutral grey. A failed payment is visually indistinguishable from a normal authorized/refunded state.

4. **Meaning rests on token text alone** — CONFIRMED. The receipt badge passes no `icon` prop (lines 174-178). StatusBadge's own doc comment (line 14-16) states meaning must be carried by "icon + text label together — never by colour alone." Here there's no icon and the text is a raw token, so for a failure the only signal is the lowercase word "failed" — no semantic color, no icon.

**Adversarial checks for refutation (all failed to refute):**
- Is it pre-existing? No — the receipt badge block is net-new in the M12 diff (`+` lines).
- Is the "other statuses use a label map" claim overstated? Partially. `UpcomingBookings` renders `whenLabel` (a date), not a status enum, and booking status is filtered upstream rather than mapped. The pre-existing `account.statusCancelled/InProgress/Pending` keys aren't wired to any M12 badge. So the specific "bookings/availability go through a label map in the diff" justification is weaker than stated — but this does NOT refute the core defect; it's still true that payment status is the lone raw-enum render and the rule-7 + color-alone problems stand on their own.
- Out of scope? No — this is an a11y + i18n defect on a screen that is the subject of the diff.

The finding is real. The supporting justification slightly overstates the "label map elsewhere" comparison, but the substantive defects (unlocalized raw enum read verbatim, rule-7 violation, and "failed" not visually distinguished with no icon) are all accurate and the suggestion is appropriate.

Summary: The receipt StatusBadge in `app/(customer)/account/page.tsx` (lines 174-178) renders the raw `payment_status` enum via `{p.status}` with no localization, confirmed newly introduced in the M12 diff. All three substantive defects check out:
